title: Adding and Subtracting Whole Numbers and Decimals
seo_title: Grade 4 Adding and Subtracting Whole Numbers and Decimals (TEKS 4.4A, STAAR)
short_title: Adding and Subtracting Whole Numbers and Decimals
standard_text: 4.4A add and subtract whole numbers and decimals to the hundredths place using the standard algorithm
meta_desc: Free Grade 4 worksheets for Texas TEKS 4.4A: add and subtract 4- to 6-digit numbers with the standard algorithm, subtract across zeros, add and subtract decimals and money, and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Line up the places. For decimals, line up the decimal points.
key_sub: Regroup when needed. Write 4.5 as 4.50 to add hundredths.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Line up the digits by place value. For decimals, line up the decimal points.
  • Add or subtract from the right. Regroup when a place has 10 or more, or when the top digit is too small.
  • Write a zero to fill an empty place: 4.5 = 4.50.

Examples

Example

4.5 + 2.37

Write 4.5 as 4.50.

4.50 + 2.37 = 6.87

Answer: 6.87

Example

6,003 − 2,458

Regroup across the zeros: 5 thousands, 9 hundreds, 9 tens, 13 ones.

13 − 8 = 5, 9 − 5 = 4, 9 − 4 = 5, 5 − 2 = 3.

Answer: 3,545

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Lining up the last digits of 4.5 and 2.37Line up the decimal points.
Forgetting to regroupCheck each place: is the top digit big enough?
Dropping a zero: 6,003 − 2,458 = 3,455Regroup across every zero.

faq.a: Add and subtract whole numbers and decimals to the hundredths place using the standard algorithm.

faq.q: Why line up the decimal points?
faq.a: So tenths are added to tenths and hundredths to hundredths.

faq.q: How do you subtract across zeros?
faq.a: Regroup from the first nonzero place: 6,003 becomes 5 thousands, 9 hundreds, 9 tens and 13 ones.

faq.q: How can I check my answer?
faq.a: Estimate by rounding, or add the difference back to the number you subtracted.

sets.title: Word problems, missing numbers and estimates

items.q: An orchard had 25,640 apples in storage. It sold 8,975 apples and then picked 6,380 more. How many apples are in storage now?
items.e: Step 1, after selling: 25,640 − 8,975 = 16,665. Step 2, after picking: 16,665 + 6,380 = 23,045. Check with estimates: 26,000 − 9,000 + 6,000 = 23,000.

items.q: An airport had 186,394 passengers in June and 207,758 passengers in July. How many passengers did it have in the two months?
items.e: Put the two months together: add. Line up the places and start with the ones. Ones: 4 + 8 = 12, write 2 and regroup 1 ten. Tens: 9 + 5 + 1 = 15, write 5 and regroup 1 hundred. Hundreds: 3 + 7 + 1 = 11, write 1 and regroup 1 thousand. Thousands: 6 + 7 + 1 = 14, write 4 and regroup 1 ten thousand. The other places add without regrouping. Answer: 394,152. Check: 394,152 − 207,758 = 186,394.
